![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/7431bd3281e4e49f4caaa5b701885fb64c58196b2256af9d8744decd9a0d0793.png)

  

Consider the diagram above, where $\overrightarrow{PS}=\mathbf{a},$ $\overrightarrow{QS}=\mathbf{b},$ $\overrightarrow{PT}=\mathbf{c},$ and $\overrightarrow{TS}=\mathbf{d}.$ Find $\overrightarrow{TQ}$ in terms of $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}, \mathbf{c},$ and $\mathbf{d}.$
e-9934.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $Q$ consisting only of the vectors $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c,$ and $\mathbf d.$

According to the triangle law of addition, 

$$
{\color{red}{\overrightarrow{TQ}}} = {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{TS}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{SQ}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/4902397acd28e2e5f85063ba55c576d3768360225a705f31a66bd460405dd5a6.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TS}} = \mathbf{d}, \qquad {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{SQ}}} = -\mathbf{b}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/08086f7e09568f908aa4919a1156d52e465216221be8908e72a1fd90ec8843dd.png)

  

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TQ} & =\overset{\to }{TS}+\overset{\to }{SQ} \\  & =d+(-b) \\  & =d-b.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4277.problem:
Consider the diagram shown below, where $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{a},$ $\overrightarrow{PT}=\mathbf{b},$ and $\overrightarrow{QS}=\mathbf{c}.$ Find $\overrightarrow{TS}$ in terms of $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},$ and $\mathbf{c}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/04ce04bf7c7f88d6578c74db0d7398a6d299d11bd9f60f4fc4b6e1bfb0129f3b.png)
e-4277.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $S$ consisting only of the vectors $\mathbf a, \mathbf b,$ or $\mathbf c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
{\color{red}{\overrightarrow{TS}}} = {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{TP}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{PQ}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{QS}}}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/53940607b5cbf0220008e6e31ec60f2fd7fd2e4f70c5a8e95e7fcfd64064b095.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TP}} = -\mathbf{b}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{PQ}} = \mathbf{a}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{QS}} = \mathbf{c}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/810cce10eb330b1767a101d9107a9534c437daa123f13056a486a9fc96dbab89.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TS} & =\overset{\to }{TP}+\overset{\to }{PQ}+\overset{\to }{QS} \\  & =-b+a+c \\  & =a-b+c.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QP}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{TP}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{TS}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RS}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QT}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
content.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/e1d5eb2f392332f69fa1507899b30b838a42ebd1c40dacddeca4edcf0f7aa8c2.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=a,\,\overset{\to }{PT}=-b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/0e8e24968141284550fac7d4e5c63333789f30ade8f7d5dd8b87fae4e012673a.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT} \\  & =a+(-b) \\  & =a-b\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\overset{\to }{XW}=\overset{\to }{XY}+\overset{\to }{YW},
$$

as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/4758b51fd3dc076059d60e944de0ad8375bb304240365959d4c6cae94f95a535.png)

$$

$$

after.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $P$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,$ and $c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{PT}=\overset{\to }{PQ}+\overset{\to }{QT},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/f5a772ed6d71bb8654fc4fc1ad6be444c6c12827b5d582cec1af18b3329ecfb9.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{PQ}=a,\,\overset{\to }{QT}=b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/ad3812200ad6af06a69d8f105c8161b7a772512a5c2ad07e12756256663f20a6.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PT} & =\overset{\to }{PQ}+\overset{\to }{QT} \\  & =a+b\end{aligned}
$$
